content.json:
### Ingestion check
Key Vault AuditEvent diagnostics record every data plane call (reads included) and the vault-level control plane calls the Key Vault RP handles itself (VaultGet/Put/Patch/Delete). The ingestion grid honours only the time range and subscription filter; everything below it honours every global filter. A vault missing from the ingestion grid but present in the ARM inventory has either had no traffic in the window or is not sending diagnostics. For live monitoring set the time range to 5 or 15 minutes and turn on auto refresh from the toolbar.

content.query:
let subSelect = dynamic([{Subscription_Filter}]);
let subNames = print SubMap = dynamic([{Sub_Map}])
| mv-expand SubMap to typeof(string)
| extend SubscriptionId = tolower(tostring(split(SubMap, '|')[0])), SubscriptionName = tostring(split(SubMap, '|')[1])
| project SubscriptionId, SubscriptionName;
AzureDiagnostics
| where TimeGenerated {Time_Range}
| where ResourceProvider == "MICROSOFT.KEYVAULT" and Category == "AuditEvent"
| where array_length(subSelect) == 0 or '*' in (subSelect) or SubscriptionId in~ (subSelect)
| summarize Events = count(), DataPlaneOps = countif(OperationName != "Authentication"), FirstEvent = min(TimeGenerated), LastEvent = max(TimeGenerated) by Vault = tolower(Resource), ResourceGroup, SubscriptionId = tolower(SubscriptionId)
| join kind=leftouter subNames on SubscriptionId
| extend MinutesSinceLast = datetime_diff('minute', now(), LastEvent)
| extend Health = case(MinutesSinceLast <= 30, "Live", MinutesSinceLast <= 360, "Idle", "No recent data")
| project Health, Vault, ResourceGroup, SubscriptionName, Events, DataPlaneOps, FirstEvent, LastEvent, MinutesSinceLast
| order by LastEvent desc
content.title: Ingestion health: AuditEvent records per vault (time and subscription filter only)

content.json:
### What the logs can and cannot tell you
Key Vault only runs the RBAC access check when the vault is on the RBAC permission model. On an access policy vault every successful call logs `isAccessPolicyMatch = true` and no RBAC evidence, regardless of what role assignments exist. So `AuthPath = AccessPolicy` means *the vault is still on access policies*, not *this identity has no RBAC path*. The pre-flip gate is `Invoke-KvRbacMigration.ps1 -Action Verify`, which expands group membership through Graph and compares against the role assignments statically.

What this tab is for:
- **Before the flip**: the active-identities grid is usage evidence. Every row must have a Group, Direct or Drop decision in the plan CSV; anything missing is a NotInPlan finding in Verify.
- **After the flip**: `isRbacAuthorized` and `appliedAssignmentId` become populated, so the granted-by grid shows which role assignment carried each call, and the ForbiddenByRbac grid shows the misses.

The inventory grid is Azure Resource Graph and is the authoritative permission model per subscription.
